scenarios.expected: Changes apply to the intended account and revoked sessions cease granting access. Unauthorized administration, invalid invites, and self/last-Administrator safeguards behave as implemented.
scenarios.actual: Organization name saved on Enter, restored on Escape and survived reloads; Default locale offered only English (United States); Default timezone is a searchable combobox that saved Europe/London; Logo accepted a PNG and refused a text file. Invite user offers exactly Legal team member, Contributor and Administrator as radio choices, so the guide now quotes the sentence-case visible label. An invitation reached Mailpit, activation through Set your password turned the row Active, and the activated Legal team member was offered no Invite user control. Re-inviting a pending address with the same role resent and left one row; with a different role it was refused with "This user already exists with a different role." and sent no mail; an activated account was refused with "This user has already activated their account."; a Portal-created Business User address was refused the same way. The Users table Role control offers four choices including Business user, appears on Active rows only, and a promoted Portal account becomes a pending Invited row that loses its role control until the resent link sets a password. Revoke all sessions ended a live session on its next request while the row stayed Active and the password still worked. Archiving blocked sign-in, Show archived plus Restore returned the account, and previously revoked sessions stayed revoked. The signed-in Administrator row offered no Archive or Revoke all sessions control, and demoting the only Administrator was refused with "You cannot demote the last Administrator." until a second Administrator was invited and activated; the demotion then applied immediately, costing the demoted session its Invite user control and returning 403 on its next request. A Contract kept its archived Owner, and only an explicit Owner reassignment through the record control moved the work before access was withdrawn.

limitations: Independent walkthroughs are agent walkthroughs, not human user studies or feature-owner approval.

Single sign-on was verified against a dedicated local OpenID Connect fixture. It is not certification of a real provider's client-secret handling or account policy, and it does not satisfy the real DocuSign and AI-provider verification required by DOC-022.

Onboarding completion is instance-wide and irreversible, so one instance permits one finishing action. Set up later on the final invitation step was exercised; Finish and the Welcome-step Set up later were not independently exercised here.
Evidence was taken on fixture app commit 6a8873dbda333fd9992eb77525d4bfa3f47af20d, not the final app candidate. DOC-025 reconciles the catalog against that candidate.
Operator and module configuration guides remain forward publication dependencies.
